proposals.argument: The DRBD board's fsx FAIL of 2026-10-21T19:36:37Z (dry-run candidate 0.90.133-2, build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, seed=3832054505, both checks failed in 2 s of an 88 s budget) is the detector failing, not MeshXFS. tests/suite/fsx.sh drew its seed from four random bytes (0..2^32-1); the vendored fsx keeps -S in an int (tests/suite/tools/fsx.c:186 'int seed = 1;', :3397 getnum) and calls usage() for a negative value (:3402-3403), exiting 90 before any operation, so neither check ran a single fsx operation on the filesystem. Reproduced host-local with the same binary: -S 3832054505 and -S 2147483648 exit 90 with the usage line; -S 2147483647 and -S 1 run (rc=0). The old draw put 10022 of 20000 seeds above INT_MAX. The detector fix is in the tree: tests/suite/fsx.sh now draws 1..2^31-1 (20000 draws, none outside) and keeps a failing check's fsx log on the node with its path in the record instead of deleting it. Nothing in the run is evidence about MeshXFS either way: fsx never opened its file.

Resubmission of P20261021-4bb0fe, which was rejected (data/reviews/P20261021-4bb0fe.md) on three points, answered here. The run: the DRBD board's fsx FAIL of 2026-10-21T19:36:37Z (dry-run candidate 0.90.133-2, build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, seed=3832054505, both checks failed in 2 s of 88 s) is the detector failing, not MeshXFS: tests/suite/fsx.sh drew its seed from 0..2^32-1, the vendored fsx keeps -S in an int (tests/suite/tools/fsx.c:186, :3397) and calls usage(), exit 90, for a negative value (:3402-3403) before it opens its file (:3493), so neither check ran an fsx operation. Reproduced host-local with the same binary (tests/evidence/fsx_seed_int_max_repro_20261021.log). (1) THE FIXED DETECTOR HAS PASSED THERE: tests/evidence/drbd_rig/criteria.runs.jsonl line 3230, 2/net/mesh/drbd fsx 2026-10-21T20:57:33Z PASS 'checks=2 passed=2 failed=0 seed=1472941388', 14 s of 88 s, run 20261021T205705Z-g2, same build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, on the fixed fsx.sh. (2) THE FIX, NAMED: the tree is uncommitted (the owner has not yet directed a commit; this session may not commit unasked), so the change is named by a hashed diff, tests/evidence/fsx_seed_fix_20261021.diff: the seed line becomes '% 2147483647 + 1' (1..2^31-1; 20000 draws, none outside, in the repro log), and a failing check keeps its log at /root/fsx.<seed>.<ops>.log on the node with fsx_fail_log=<host>:<path> in the run's measured field and its tail in the kernel log, instead of the old /tmp file the EXIT trap deleted. On the record's own next step (logs under the run's evidence): the node's log stays where the run names it; run.sh copying it into tests/evidence is not part of this fix. (3) THE RECORD: D-FSX-RANDOM-SEED-ABOVE-INT-MAX-MAKES-FSX-EXIT-WITH-USAGE-AND-LOGS-ARE-DELETED names this run in its cells; a detector-defect proposal carries no --record (tools/defects.py takes a record only for record proposals), so it is named here.

The owner was asked (2026-10-22, recorded verbatim as the last owner_approved entry of data/release_policy.json) to choose between approving an exception for this record in data/release_policy.json and holding 0.90.134 for the IPMI fence work. The owner answered 'leave the DRBD work for .135/.136': 0.90.134 does not wait for the DRBD fence work, so the record is excepted for 0.90.134 at 2/net/mesh/drbd only, the configuration it reaches. The policy's exceptions entry names exactly this record, 2/net/mesh/drbd and release 0.90.134. Nothing else about the record changes: it stays open with impact stability, reach 2 nodes */*/drbd, its evidence and its next step, and it blocks 2/net/mesh/drbd in every other release (tools/defects.py owner_exception and excepted_here: an excepted_at mark counts only for its candidate and only while the policy still grants it).

This proposal settles 3/disk/caw/direct:guard_census:2026-10-11T00:56:39Z. The run's FAIL was the census tool's fault, not MeshXFS's. tests/tooling/guard_census.sh runs tools/sole_survivor_audit.py --check against tests/criteria/sole_survivor_sites.json and fails when it reads any guard as new or grown (guard_census.sh:61-70). On 2026-10-11 the audit credited each single-node guard to the last column-0 'name(' above it and counted MODULE_PARM_DESC(, module_param_named( and EXPORT_SYMBOL( as names; 0.90.118 added the ag_nb_mute_unanswered_master module parameter between v5_boot_k_lineage and mxfs_v5_dlm_is_mds(), which re-credited that already reviewed guard to MODULE_PARM_DESC, so the census read it as new (measured 'new=1 grown=0') on every configuration that ran it that evening: 3/disk/caw/direct 00:56:39Z, 3/net/mesh/direct 00:58:17Z, 5/disk/caw/direct 00:58:14Z and 5/net/mesh/direct 01:01:56Z (data/criteria.runs.jsonl:1349, :1359, :1357, :1372). The detector fix is in the tree: tools/sole_survivor_audit.py:58-62 (NOT_FUNC skips column-0 MODULE_*, module_param* and EXPORT_SYMBOL* invocations), described in CHANGELOG.md:3881-3891 (0.90.119); the file's mtime is 2026-10-11T01:02:44Z, after the four FAILs and before the next runs. Independent evidence that the code did the right thing: the guard the census flagged is the reviewed inventory entry, and the same configurations' guard_census passed on the fixed detector minutes later with nothing else changed (data/criteria.runs.jsonl:1377 3/disk/caw/direct 01:05:18Z PASS, :1379 3/net/mesh/direct 01:05:26Z PASS, :1381 5/disk/caw/direct 01:05:36Z PASS, :1384 5/net/mesh/direct 01:06:48Z PASS, build A969E000AECBD63CBC36F81), as has every guard_census run since. The sweep that collected these lines is tests/evidence/incident_remaining_evidence_20261023.txt:2010-2146.

The release build step of the 0.90.133-2 dry run failed before building anything: its whole-tree rsync could not read a root-only result file, tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.build.log:2 'rsync: [sender] send_files failed to open "/home/steve/src/mxfs/bench.json": Permission denied (13)', :4 '=== rc=23', recorded as data/criteria.runs.jsonl:6836 'could not copy the tree'. That is the step's own fault (the detector): bench.json is a benchmark result, not a frozen input, and nothing about the candidate's module or tools was measured. The detector fix is in the tree: tools/release_run.py:229-238, the build copies the candidate's frozen file list only (rsync --files-from of the manifest's files), with the comment naming this failure; CHANGELOG.md 0.90.133 entry, 'The clean build copied the whole tree and stopped on a root-only result file. It now copies the candidate's frozen file list and nothing else'. Independent evidence that the candidate built: the next build step on the same module 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A passed on the fixed detector (data/criteria.runs.jsonl:6943, 2026-10-21T20:49:59Z, 'clean build 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A, tools, tauth, audits'), and every build step since passed (:6962, :7053, :7144). Collected in tests/evidence/incident_remaining_evidence_20261023.txt:2701-2718.

The packages step of the 0.90.133-2 dry run failed in the platform build check, before any package was built, because the rig's Proxmox build VM lacked the kernel headers for one claimed kernel: tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.packages.log:10 'VM_KBUILD_FAIL pve9 pve9-1 7.0.14-24-pve (no headers for 7.0.14-24-pve installed on pve9-1)', :11 'NO_HEADERS 7.0.14-24-pve', :12 'ERROR: ... failed; no packages built' (scripts/vm_kbuild_check.sh:74 prints NO_HEADERS when the VM has no $hdr/Makefile for that kernel, :91). The same check built MeshXFS on that VM for the other kernels in the same step (:6 VM_KBUILD_OK ... 7.0.14-19-pve, :8 VM_KBUILD_OK ... 6.17.2-1-pve), so the build itself was sound; the missing header package is the VM's state, outside MeshXFS, and it precedes the failure. Once the headers were on the VM the identical check passed for that kernel: tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.134_20261021T212712Z.packages.log:6 'VM_KBUILD_OK pve9 pve9-1 7.0.14-24-pve C0589CD3CE0FFA63297F6A8' (2026-10-21T21:27Z) and 0.90.134_20261021T230333Z.packages.log:6, and the packages step passed at data/criteria.runs.jsonl:7055 (2026-10-21T23:30:01Z, '3 packages in dist/0.90.134'). No MeshXFS kernel line is involved: nothing was loaded or mounted in this step. Collected in tests/evidence/incident_remaining_evidence_20261023.txt:2719-2743.

The platforms step of the 0.90.133-2 dry run had no packages to verify, because the packages step before it had failed on the build VM's missing kernel headers (tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.packages.log:10-12, 'VM_KBUILD_FAIL pve9 pve9-1 7.0.14-24-pve (no headers for 7.0.14-24-pve installed on pve9-1)' ... 'no packages built'; data/candidates/0.90.133-2.json:46-52 packages failed). tests/full_verify.sh then refused before running a round: tests/evidence/candidates/0.90.133-2.platforms.log:2 'PLATFORMS leaves out pve9, which has no run of 0.90.133-2 to be graded on', :3 '=== rc=2', recorded as data/criteria.runs.jsonl:6911 'full_verify platforms rc=2, -1 failed step(s)'. No package was installed and no node ran MeshXFS in this step, so it measured nothing of MeshXFS; its cause is the same infrastructure fault, outside MeshXFS, that preceded it. The step now refuses outright when the packages step did not pass (tools/release_run.py:489-493, comment naming 0.90.133-2), and with packages present it passed: data/criteria.runs.jsonl:7129 (2026-10-22T01:55:36Z, "every released platform's packaged round and hung-node test"). Collected in tests/evidence/incident_remaining_evidence_20261023.txt:2780-2793.
